scenario: 广告 CTR 预测模型上线前后都要评估；CTR = 一次曝光被点击的概率，模型给每个候选广告打这个分。
scenario_en: An ad CTR model must be evaluated before and after launch; CTR is the probability an impression gets clicked, and the model scores each candidate ad.
q: 为什么广告 CTR 模型要「离线 + 在线」两阶段评估，各把什么关？
q_en: Why evaluate an ad CTR model in two phases, offline and online, and what does each gate check?
why: 离线只能验证模型本身「排序准不准、概率准不准」，测不出收入、体验退化或反馈回路；在线 A/B 才把模型质量翻译成业务影响。排序再漂亮，概率没校准照样在竞价里亏钱。
why_en: Offline checks whether the model ranks and calibrates well, but only online A/B tells you if that translates into revenue and UX, since a well-ranking but miscalibrated model can still lose money in the auction.
diagram:
flowchart LR O["离线关
AUC / log loss / 校准"] --> A["在线 A/B
RPM + 体验护栏"] A --> F["公平/合规关
人群交付审计"]
options: 只需离线评估——AUC、log loss 达标就能保证线上收入，在线 A/B 是浪费流量
只需在线 A/B——直接看真实收入最可信，离线指标和钱无关，可以跳过
离线守模型质量（排序 + 概率校准），在线 A/B 守收入与体验的真实影响
离线测收入、在线测模型精度，两者测的是同一件事，只是运行环境不同
options_en: Offline evaluation alone suffices — good AUC and log loss guarantee online revenue, so A/B testing just wastes traffic.
Online A/B alone suffices — real revenue is most trustworthy, and offline metrics have nothing to do with money, so skip them.
Offline guards model quality (ranking plus calibration); online A/B guards real revenue and UX impact.
Offline measures revenue and online measures model accuracy; they test the same thing in different environments.
optionExplanations: 离线指标测不出收入曲线、体验退化和反馈回路，达标的模型上线照样可能亏，所以不能省在线关。
跳过离线等于让所有坏模型都用真实流量试错，代价是真金白银的收入和用户体验。
对；离线守模型质量、在线守业务影响、之后再守公平合规，三道关各测不同的失败面。
两者测的不是同一件事：离线看模型内在质量，在线看它对业务的因果影响。
optionExplanations_en: Offline metrics cannot see the revenue curve, UX regressions, or feedback loops, so a passing model can still lose money live — you cannot drop the online gate.
Skipping offline means every bad model burns real traffic to fail, costing actual revenue and user experience.
Correct — offline guards model quality, online guards business impact, then fairness guards compliance; each gate catches a different failure surface.
They do not test the same thing: offline sees intrinsic quality, online sees causal business impact.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：一次广告曝光被点击的概率，是 CTR 模型要预测的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the probability that an ad impression is clicked, the target a CTR model predicts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把流量随机切成对照组和实验组，比较新旧模型的真实业务指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An A/B test randomly splits traffic into control and treatment to compare real business metrics of old vs new models.

scenario: 离线评估一个 CTR 模型，你想先确认它「谁更可能被点」这件事排得对不对。
scenario_en: You are offline-evaluating a CTR model and first want to confirm it ranks 'who is more likely to click' correctly.
q: AUC-ROC 到底测什么？它的盲区是什么？
q_en: What does AUC-ROC actually measure, and what is its blind spot?
why: AUC-ROC 测排序区分度：随机取一个正样本（点击）和一个负样本，模型给正样本更高分的概率。它对绝对概率不敏感——排序全对但预测值整体偏高偏低，AUC 照样漂亮。
why_en: AUC-ROC measures ranking discrimination — the chance the model scores a random click above a random non-click — and is insensitive to absolute probabilities, so a well-ranked but systematically over/under-confident model still scores well.
tradeoff: AUC（排序对不对）vs log loss/校准（概率准不准）
options: AUC 测排序区分度，对绝对概率不敏感，看不出校准偏差
AUC 直接测预测概率和真实点击率的偏差，是校准是否准确的主指标
AUC 测的是预测值的绝对误差，越接近 0 说明每条预测的概率越准
AUC 越高一定说明概率校准越好，可以单独用它决定模型能否上线
options_en: AUC measures ranking discrimination and is blind to absolute probabilities, so calibration bias is invisible to it.
AUC directly measures the gap between predicted probability and observed click rate, and is the primary calibration metric.
AUC measures absolute error of predictions, and values near 0 mean each predicted probability is accurate.
Higher AUC always means better calibration, so it alone can decide whether a model ships.
optionExplanations: 对；AUC 只关心相对顺序，把所有预测同乘一个常数排序不变、AUC 不变，所以它测不出概率偏差。
混淆了指标：测预测概率和观测点击率偏差的是校准曲线/log loss，不是 AUC。
AUC 不是绝对误差指标；它对预测值整体缩放完全不敏感。
AUC 高只代表排序好；概率校准要另测，单看 AUC 会放行一个在竞价里算错钱的模型。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — AUC cares only about relative order; scaling all predictions by a constant leaves ranking and AUC unchanged, so it cannot detect probability bias.
Metric mix-up: measuring predicted vs observed rate is calibration curves / log loss, not AUC.
AUC is not an absolute-error metric; it is fully insensitive to overall scaling of predictions.
High AUC only means good ranking; calibration must be measured separately, and shipping on AUC alone lets through a model that misprices the auction.

termDefinitions.fullName: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve
termDefinitions.meaning: 受试者工作特征曲线下面积：衡量模型把正样本排在负样本前面的能力，0.5=瞎猜，1=完美排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC-ROC (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve) measures how well a model ranks positives above negatives, where 0.5 is random and 1 is perfect.

scenario: 同一个 CTR 模型 AUC 很高，但你怀疑它预测的概率整体偏离真实点击率。
scenario_en: A CTR model has high AUC but you suspect its predicted probabilities are systematically off from the true click rate.
q: log loss（交叉熵）补上了 AUC 的什么盲区？它自己又有什么弱点？
q_en: What blind spot of AUC does log loss (cross-entropy) fill, and what is its own weakness?
why: log loss 惩罚预测概率和真实标签的偏差，对校准敏感——AUC 高但 log loss 差就说明模型过/欠自信，会扭曲竞价经济。弱点：类别极不平衡时（点击稀少），它容易被多数类（未点击）主导。
why_en: Log loss penalizes the gap between predicted probability and label, so it is calibration-sensitive and flags an over/under-confident model that high AUC hides; its weakness is that under heavy class imbalance the majority (non-click) class dominates it.
options: log loss 只测排序，和 AUC 完全等价，两个指标可以互相替代
log loss 对概率校准不敏感，主要用来测模型的推理延迟
log loss 只在类别完全平衡时有意义，CTR 这种稀疏点击场景根本不能用
log loss 对校准敏感，能抓过/欠自信；但类别极不平衡时易被多数类主导
options_en: Log loss only measures ranking and is fully equivalent to AUC, so they are interchangeable.
Log loss is insensitive to calibration and is mainly used to measure inference latency.
Log loss is meaningful only under perfectly balanced classes and cannot be used for sparse-click CTR at all.
Log loss is calibration-sensitive and catches over/under-confidence, but under heavy imbalance the majority class dominates it.
optionExplanations: 两者不等价：AUC 只看排序，log loss 看概率数值，正是它抓住了 AUC 看不见的校准偏差。
恰恰相反，log loss 对校准非常敏感；延迟是服务侧的事，和这个损失无关。
不平衡会让它偏向多数类，但仍可用（配合类别加权/校准曲线），不是「根本不能用」。
对；它数值化了「概率准不准」，代价是稀疏点击时未点击样本会摊薄信号，需配合校准曲线看分段。
optionExplanations_en: Not equivalent: AUC sees only ranking, log loss sees the probability value, which is exactly the calibration bias AUC misses.
Opposite — log loss is highly calibration-sensitive; latency is a serving concern unrelated to this loss.
Imbalance biases it toward the majority class but it is still usable (with class weighting / calibration curves), not unusable.
Correct — it quantifies whether probabilities are right, at the cost that sparse clicks let non-click samples dilute the signal, so pair it with per-segment calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对数损失/交叉熵：预测概率越偏离真实标签、惩罚越大，是概率校准的核心离线指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Log loss (cross-entropy) grows as predicted probability diverges from the label, and is the core offline metric for probability calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 正负样本数量悬殊；CTR 里点击（正）远少于未点击（负）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Class imbalance is a large skew between positive and negative counts; in CTR clicks (positives) are far rarer than non-clicks.

scenario: 你想直观检查 CTR 模型「预测 20% 的那批广告，真实点击率是不是也接近 20%」。
scenario_en: You want to visually check whether ads the CTR model predicts at 20% actually get clicked near 20% of the time.
q: 校准曲线（reliability diagram）是怎么画、怎么读的？
q_en: How is a calibration curve (reliability diagram) built and read?
why: 把预测概率按大小分箱（如十分位），每箱画「平均预测概率 vs 实际点击率」，看是否贴近 45° 对角线；偏离说明过/欠自信，用来验证 Platt scaling / isotonic 等校准是否生效。
why_en: Bin predictions by magnitude (e.g. deciles), plot mean predicted probability against observed click rate per bin, and check closeness to the 45-degree diagonal, which verifies whether Platt scaling or isotonic correction worked.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  P["预测概率"] --> B["按十分位分箱"]
  B --> C["每箱: 平均预测 vs 实际点击率"]
  C --> D["贴 45° 对角线? 偏离=过/欠自信"]
options: 把广告按点击与否分两堆，比较两堆的平均预测分，差距越大说明校准越好
按预测概率分箱，画每箱平均预测 vs 实际点击率，看是否贴近对角线
画 ROC 曲线，看曲线下面积是否接近 1，越接近说明概率越准
统计每天总点击数随时间的变化曲线，用趋势是否平稳判断校准
options_en: Split ads into clicked and non-clicked piles and compare mean predicted scores, where a bigger gap means better calibration.
Bin by predicted probability, plot mean predicted versus observed click rate per bin, and check closeness to the diagonal.
Draw the ROC curve and check whether the area under it nears 1, since closer means more accurate probabilities.
Plot total daily clicks over time and judge calibration by whether the trend looks stable.
optionExplanations: 这是排序类思路（类似 AUC 的正负分离），不检验预测概率的数值是否等于真实频率。
对；分箱后对角线检验的是「预测 p 的那批，实际频率是不是也 p」，正是校准的定义。
那是 AUC-ROC 的画法，测排序不测校准，看不出概率是否偏高偏低。
总点击趋势是业务监控，和单条预测概率是否校准无关。
optionExplanations_en: That is a ranking-style idea (like AUC's positive/negative separation) and does not check whether predicted probability equals observed frequency.
Correct — the diagonal check on bins tests whether ads predicted at p really occur at frequency p, which is the definition of calibration.
That is the AUC-ROC construction, which measures ranking not calibration and cannot see probability bias.
Total click trend is business monitoring, unrelated to whether individual predicted probabilities are calibrated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 校准曲线/可靠性图：按预测概率分箱后画预测 vs 实际频率，越贴对角线越校准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A calibration curve (reliability diagram) bins predictions and plots predicted vs observed frequency; closer to the diagonal means better calibrated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两种事后校准方法：Platt 用逻辑回归重映概率，isotonic 用单调分段函数拟合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Platt scaling and isotonic regression are post-hoc calibration methods: Platt refits probabilities with logistic regression, isotonic fits a monotonic step function.

scenario: 竞价系统按「预测 CTR × 出价」算期望收入排广告，所以概率数值直接决定谁赢；你要选离线指标同时守住排序和概率两个维度。
scenario_en: The auction ranks ads by predicted CTR times bid, so the probability value decides who wins, and you must pick offline metrics that guard both ranking and probability.
q: 该用哪一组离线指标覆盖排序质量 + 概率质量？
q_en: Which set of offline metrics covers both ranking quality and probability quality?
why: 「AUC 管排序、log loss + 校准曲线管概率」正好覆盖面试官必问的两个维度。只看 AUC 会放行算错期望收入的模型；只看 log loss 又难定位是哪段概率偏了，校准曲线补上分段视角。
why_en: Use AUC for ranking and log loss plus calibration curves for probability, covering both dimensions interviewers probe, since AUC alone ships a model that misprices expected revenue.
tradeoff: AUC（排序）vs log loss + 校准曲线（概率数值 + 分段定位）
whenOtherWins: 如果下游只用排序、完全不用概率数值（如纯 top-1 展示、不进竞价算钱），那 AUC 单独够用，log loss 可以次要。
options: 只用 AUC——排序对了，竞价里赢家顺序不会错，概率数值大小不影响谁中标
只用 log loss——它已经综合了整体概率误差，校准曲线只是换种方式看同一件事
AUC 管排序，log loss + 校准曲线管概率，两维一起看
只用 SERP CTR 一个线上指标，离线跑起来费时又滞后，不如上线看真实效果
options_en: Use AUC only — if ranking is right, the auction's winner order will not be wrong, and probability magnitude does not affect who wins.
Use log loss only — it already aggregates overall probability error, and a calibration curve is just another way to look at the same thing.
AUC for ranking, log loss plus calibration curves for probability — evaluate both dimensions together.
Use only SERP CTR as one online metric — offline runs take time and lag behind, so just check the real result after launch.
optionExplanations: 竞价按 CTR×出价算钱，排序对但概率偏高，仍会给低质广告灌高期望收入，AUC 看不见。
log loss 给一个总分，但分不清是哪段概率偏了；校准曲线的分箱视角才能定位。
对；两指标分工明确，AUC 守排序、log loss+校准守概率数值，正好压住竞价对概率的依赖。
线上指标不能在放量前拦住坏模型；离线关的意义就是先验证再放流量。
optionExplanations_en: The auction prices by CTR times bid, so right ranking with inflated probability still gives low-quality ads high expected revenue, which AUC cannot see.
Log loss gives one aggregate but cannot localize which probability range is off; the calibration curve's bins can.
Correct — clear division of labor: AUC guards ranking, log loss plus calibration guard probability values, matching the auction's reliance on probability.
Online metrics cannot stop a bad model before rollout; the offline gate exists to validate before spending traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 竞价排序依据，约等于 预测 CTR × 出价；概率偏高会虚高期望收入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Expected revenue is the auction ranking basis, roughly predicted CTR times bid, so inflated probability inflates it.

scenario: 整体校准曲线贴合 45° 对角线看着很好，但你怀疑某些广告品类/设备/地区上概率是偏的。
scenario_en: The aggregate calibration curve hugs the diagonal, but you suspect probabilities are biased on certain ad categories, devices, or geos.
q: 整体校准良好，为什么还要按品类/设备/地区分段看校准？
q_en: If aggregate calibration looks good, why still evaluate calibration per ad category, device, and geo?
why: 聚合校准会互相抵消——某品类高估、另一品类低估，平均后看起来对齐，掩盖了分段问题。分段校准能暴露局部过/欠自信，避免在某个细分市场系统性算错竞价。
why_en: Aggregate calibration can cancel out — one segment over-predicts while another under-predicts — hiding local bias, so per-segment calibration exposes where the model is quietly mispricing.
options: 分段没必要——大盘对角线已经贴合，说明模型整体无偏，不必再拆样本重复验证
聚合会互相抵消（一段高估、一段低估），分段才暴露局部偏差
分段只是把同一份大盘数据切碎了看，报表更好看而已，对竞价定价没有额外信息
分段本质是想提升模型的排序 AUC，和概率是否校准这件事没有关系
options_en: Segmentation is unnecessary — the aggregate diagonal already fits, meaning the model is unbiased overall, so there's no need to re-slice samples.
Aggregation cancels out — one segment over-predicts, another under-predicts — so only per-segment views expose local bias.
Segmentation just slices the same aggregate data into smaller pieces, making reports look nicer, with no extra signal for auction pricing.
Segmentation is essentially about raising the model's ranking AUC, and has nothing to do with whether probabilities are calibrated.
optionExplanations: 整体对齐可能是相反偏差抵消的假象，某品类系统性高估的钱照样亏。
对；分段暴露被平均掩盖的局部偏差，避免在某设备或地区细分市场持续算错期望收入。
这不是报表美观问题——分段偏差直接对应某细分市场的竞价定价错误。
校准和 AUC 是两回事；分段看的是概率是否局部偏，不是排序。
optionExplanations_en: A good aggregate can be an illusion from opposite biases canceling, so a systematically over-predicting segment still loses money.
Correct — segmentation exposes local bias hidden by averaging, avoiding persistent mispricing in a device or geo segment.
This is not about pretty reports — segment bias maps directly to auction mispricing in that segment.
Calibration and AUC are different; segmentation checks local probability bias, not ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按品类、设备、地区分别检查校准，暴露被整体平均掩盖的局部概率偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Segment calibration checks calibration per category, device, or geo to reveal local probability bias hidden by aggregation.

scenario: 模型 AUC 0.82（排序不错），但系统性过自信，预测点击率比真实高约 15 个百分点，竞价用第二价格拍卖（赢家付第二高者的价）。
scenario_en: A model has AUC 0.82 (decent ranking) but is systematically overconfident, predicting click rate about 15 points above actual, in a second-price auction (winner pays the runner-up's price).
q: 排序不错但过自信，在第二价格竞价里会造成什么后果？
q_en: With good ranking but overconfidence, what happens in a second-price auction?
why: 竞价按 预测CTR×出价 排期望收入，过自信把某些广告的期望收入吹高，让本该输的低质广告赢下它们不该赢的位置。这正是「AUC 高但校准差会扭曲竞价经济」的具体表现。
why_en: The auction ranks by predicted CTR times bid, and overconfidence inflates some ads' expected revenue so low-quality ads win slots they should lose, which is exactly how good AUC with bad calibration distorts auction economics.
options: 没有影响：第二价格拍卖会自动抵消概率偏差，赢家不变
排序整体变差，AUC 会跌到 0.5 附近
低质广告期望收入被虚高，赢下本该输的位置
所有广告的实际点击率都会随之升高 15 个百分点
options_en: No impact: a second-price auction automatically cancels probability bias and the winner is unchanged.
Overall ranking degrades and AUC drops toward 0.5.
Low-quality ads get inflated expected revenue and win slots they should lose.
Every ad's actual click rate rises by 15 points as a result.
optionExplanations: 第二价格只改「付多少」，不改「谁赢」；谁赢由期望收入排序决定，过自信照样带偏。
过自信是概率整体偏移，排序（AUC）基本不变，恰恰是 AUC 看不见这个问题。
对；虚高的期望收入让低质广告排到前面，赢下不该赢的位，长期拉低平台真实收益与体验。
预测偏高不会改变真实点击率，只会改变竞价排序和定价。
optionExplanations_en: Second-price only changes what you pay, not who wins; the winner is set by expected-revenue ranking, which overconfidence still skews.
Overconfidence is an overall probability shift, so ranking (AUC) barely moves — which is why AUC cannot see it.
Correct — inflated expected revenue ranks low-quality ads too high, letting them win undeserved slots and hurting real revenue and UX over time.
Over-prediction does not change actual click rate; it only changes auction ranking and pricing.

termDefinitions.term: second-price auction / 第二价格拍卖
termDefinitions.meaning: 赢家按第二高者的出价付费；决定谁赢的仍是各家的期望收入排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In a second-price auction the winner pays the runner-up's bid, but who wins is still set by expected-revenue ranking.

q: 补全 CTR 离线评估的两维口诀：
q_en: Fill in the two-dimension mnemonic for offline CTR evaluation.
text: 排序质量看 {{AUC}}（对绝对概率不敏感）；概率质量看 {{log loss}} + {{校准曲线}}（分段看是否贴 45° 对角线）。
text_en: For ranking quality use {{AUC}} (insensitive to absolute probability); for probability quality use {{log loss}} plus {{calibration curves}} (check the 45-degree diagonal per segment).
why: 一句话记住分工：AUC 只保证排序对，概率是否可信要靠 log loss 和校准曲线，二者缺一都会在竞价里算错钱。
why_en: AUC guarantees only ranking, while whether probabilities are trustworthy needs log loss and calibration curves, and missing either misprices the auction.

scenario: 新 CTR 模型离线达标，要做线上 A/B 和生产基线比。你要选一个「主指标」代表广告业务的核心收益。
scenario_en: A new CTR model passed offline and needs an online A/B against the production baseline; you must pick a primary metric representing core ad-business value.
q: 线上 A/B 该用哪个指标当收入主指标？
q_en: Which metric should be the revenue primary metric for the online A/B?
why: 主指标用 RPM（每千次曝光收入），因为它把「点击率 × 单价 × 展示量」压成一个可比的收益率，直接对齐广告业务目标；单看点击数或点击率会忽略每次点击值多少钱。
why_en: Use RPM (revenue per mille) as the primary metric because it compresses click rate, price, and volume into one comparable yield aligned with the ad business, whereas raw clicks ignore how much each click is worth.
tradeoff: RPM（收益率，含单价）vs 纯点击率（只看点击、忽略每次点击的价值）
whenOtherWins: 如果实验目标是纯用户参与（如信息流点击体验），而非直接变现，那用点击率/参与度当主指标更贴目标。
options: 总曝光数：曝光越多说明系统越健康、库存利用越充分
模型 AUC：线上继续看排序质量，最能反映模型好坏
点击总数：点得越多说明广告越成功，直接反映收入
RPM（每千次曝光收入）：把点击率与单价压成可比收益率
options_en: Total impressions: more impressions means a healthier system with better inventory utilization.
Model AUC: keep watching ranking quality online, as it best reflects model quality.
Total clicks: more clicks means more successful ads, directly reflecting revenue.
RPM (revenue per mille): compresses click rate and price into one comparable yield.
optionExplanations: 曝光数是产能不是收益，堆曝光反而可能靠塞广告刷出来，伤体验。
AUC 是离线排序指标，A/B 要测的是真实业务影响，不是继续看排序。
点击数忽略每次点击值多少钱：一堆廉价点击可能不如少量高价点击赚钱。
对；RPM 直接对齐变现目标，是广告 A/B 的标准主指标，再配体验护栏。
optionExplanations_en: Impressions are capacity not yield, and pumping them may just mean stuffing more ads, hurting UX.
AUC is an offline ranking metric; A/B must measure real business impact, not keep watching ranking.
Click count ignores what each click is worth: many cheap clicks may earn less than a few high-value ones.
Correct — RPM aligns directly with monetization and is the standard ad-A/B primary metric, paired with UX guardrails.

termDefinitions.fullName: Revenue Per Mille (revenue per thousand impressions)
termDefinitions.meaning: 每千次曝光收入：广告变现的核心收益率指标，A/B 的收入主指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPM (Revenue Per Mille) is revenue per thousand impressions, the core monetization yield and A/B primary metric.

scenario: 同一个用户一天会跨多个会话看到广告；你要给 CTR 模型 A/B 选切分粒度。
scenario_en: The same user sees ads across multiple sessions in a day; you must choose the A/B split unit for the CTR model.
q: A/B 该按什么粒度切分流量：会话级还是用户级？
q_en: At what granularity should you split A/B traffic: session-level or user-level?
why: 按用户级切分：同一用户固定在一组，跨会话行为不会污染归因。统计单位 = 独立用户数（不是会话数），会话级样本看着多但彼此相关，会高估功效。
why_en: Split at the user level so one user always stays in one arm; the unit of analysis is distinct users, not sessions, because sessions from the same person are correlated and inflate apparent power.
tradeoff: 用户级（同一人固定一组、干净归因）vs 会话级（同人跨组、跨会话污染）
whenOtherWins: 只有当效应严格限于单次会话内、且用户跨会话行为完全无关时，会话级切分才不会污染——广告场景几乎不满足。
options: 会话级：粒度更细，样本量更大，统计更快到显著
用户级：同一用户固定在一组，避免跨会话污染
请求级：每个广告请求独立随机分组，最灵活
地区级：按城市分组，天然隔离最彻底
options_en: Session-level: finer granularity and a larger sample reach significance faster.
User-level: a user stays in one arm, avoiding cross-session contamination.
Request-level: randomize each ad request independently, most flexible.
Geo-level: split by city, the most thoroughly isolated.
optionExplanations: 会话级样本是多了，但同一用户在两组间跳会把两组行为互相污染，归因不再干净。
对；用户级把「同一人只属于一组」钉死，切断跨会话污染，收入差才可信。
请求级污染更严重：同一用户同一会话内都可能横跨两组，无法干净归因。
地区级隔离过粗，城市间本身差异大，会把地域差混进实验效应。
optionExplanations_en: Session-level adds samples, but a user flipping between arms cross-contaminates their behavior and breaks clean attribution.
Correct — user-level pins one person to one arm, cutting cross-session contamination so the revenue delta is trustworthy.
Request-level contaminates more: even one session can straddle both arms, preventing clean attribution.
Geo-level is too coarse; cities differ intrinsically, folding geographic variance into the treatment effect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一用户在不同会话被分到不同实验组，两组行为互相影响，破坏归因。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-session contamination is when a user lands in different arms across sessions, so behaviors bleed between groups and break attribution.

scenario: 团队想周一到周五跑完 CTR 模型 A/B 就下结论上线。
scenario_en: The team wants to run the CTR A/B Monday to Friday and conclude/ship.
q: A/B 只跑工作日（周一到周五）会有什么风险？
q_en: What is the risk of running the A/B only on weekdays (Mon-Fri)?
why: 实验时长必须覆盖完整的星期几周期 + 季节性，工作日和周末的用户行为与广告需求差别很大；只跑周一到周五会漏掉周末模式，得出偏颇结论。
why_en: Duration must span the full day-of-week cycle and seasonality, since weekday and weekend behavior differ, so a Mon-Fri-only test misses weekend patterns and gives a biased conclusion.
options: 漏掉周末行为模式，结论对整周不成立
没有风险，工作日样本足够代表所有情况
唯一影响是样本量偏小，把每天流量翻倍即可解决
只会让统计功效略降，不影响结论方向和上线决策
options_en: It misses weekend behavior, so the conclusion does not hold for a full week.
No risk — weekday samples fully represent all situations.
The only effect is a smaller sample, fixable by doubling daily traffic.
It only slightly lowers statistical power without changing the conclusion or the launch decision.
optionExplanations: 对；周末的浏览时长、购买意图、广告品类需求都变了，漏掉它会系统性偏，上线后打脸。
工作日不能代表周末，二者行为分布不同，属于覆盖不全不是随机噪声。
翻倍流量补的是样本量，补不了「时间维度覆盖不全」这个系统性偏差。
这是分布偏差不只是功效问题，可能直接把结论方向带反。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — weekend dwell time, purchase intent, and category demand differ, so omitting it biases systematically and backfires live.
Weekdays cannot represent weekends; their behavior distributions differ, a coverage gap not random noise.
Doubling traffic adds samples but cannot fix the systematic bias of incomplete time coverage.
This is a distribution bias, not just power, and can flip the conclusion's direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 行为随星期几、节假日、季度周期性波动；实验时长要覆盖完整周期才有代表性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Seasonality is periodic behavior variation by weekday, holiday, or quarter, so tests must span a full cycle to be representative.

scenario: CTR 模型 A/B 只盯 RPM 会危险：一个模型可能靠多塞广告短期抬收入却赶跑用户。你要设一组护栏指标。
scenario_en: Watching only RPM in a CTR A/B is risky: a model can pump short-term revenue by stuffing ads while driving users away, so you set guardrail metrics.
q: 哪些应作为广告 A/B 的护栏指标？(多选)
q_en: Which should be guardrail metrics for an ad A/B? (multiple)
why: 护栏指标监控主指标之外的副作用：每会话广告负载（塞太多广告短期抬收入、长期流失）、会话时长/回访率（下降=产品体验退化）、负反馈（隐藏/举报/静音）。模型训练速度不是业务护栏。
why_en: Guardrails watch side effects beyond the primary metric: ad load per session, session length and return rate, and negative feedback, while training speed is not a business guardrail.
options: 每会话广告负载（塞太多广告短期抬收入、长期赶跑用户）
会话时长 + 回访率（下降说明产品体验在退化）
负反馈率（隐藏、举报、静音广告的比例）
模型的训练收敛速度（多少小时训完）
options_en: Ad load per session (too many ads lift short-term revenue but drive users away long-term).
Session length and return rate (drops signal product-experience degradation).
Negative feedback rate (share of hides, reports, mutes).
Model training convergence speed (hours to train).
optionExplanations: 对；广告负载是典型的短期收入 vs 长期留存陷阱，必须护栏住。
对；会话时长和回访率下滑是产品退化的早期信号，收入涨也要拦。
对；隐藏/举报/静音是用户对广告不满的直接表达，升高就该警惕。
错；训练速度是工程效率指标，和用户体验/业务风险无关，不是护栏。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — ad load is the classic short-term-revenue vs long-term-retention trap and must be guarded.
Correct — falling session length and return rate are early signs of product degradation, blocking even a revenue win.
Correct — hides, reports, and mutes directly express ad dissatisfaction and should trigger caution when rising.
Incorrect — training speed is an engineering-efficiency metric, unrelated to UX or business risk, not a guardrail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 除主指标外必须不退化的副作用指标，任一越界即拒绝上线，即使主指标变好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a side-effect metric that must not regress; breaching any one rejects the launch even if the primary metric improves.

scenario: 新模型 A/B 里 RPM +2%（主指标涨），但会话时长明显下滑、负反馈率超过阈值。
scenario_en: In the A/B the new model shows RPM +2% (primary up), but session length clearly drops and negative-feedback rate exceeds threshold.
q: 主指标涨了 +2%，但护栏退化超阈值，该不该上线？
q_en: The primary is up 2% but a guardrail breaches threshold — should you ship?
why: 拒绝上线：护栏越界代表这 +2% 收入是靠伤害体验换来的，长期会流失用户、反噬收入。护栏的作用就是给主指标设否决权，防止短期收益掩盖长期损害。
why_en: Reject the launch — a breached guardrail means the 2% came at the cost of UX that will churn users and reverse the gain long-term, since guardrails hold veto power over the primary metric.
tradeoff: 短期 +2% RPM vs 体验退化带来的长期流失与收入反噬
whenOtherWins: 若护栏只是轻微、可解释的短期波动（如新体验的学习期）且已确认会回弹，可在密切监控下小流量放量再复核。
options: 上线：主指标涨了就是成功信号，护栏退化可以放量之后再慢慢优化
上线：+2% 收入是实打实的硬指标，护栏那点波动大概率只是噪声
拒绝上线：护栏越界说明收入是拿体验换的，长期会反噬
折中：先只对高价值用户群体上线新模型，其余用户继续留旧模型观察
options_en: Ship: the primary going up is a success signal, and the guardrail regression can be optimized later after rollout.
Ship: +2% revenue is a hard, real number, and that guardrail wobble is most likely just noise.
Reject: a breached guardrail means revenue was bought with UX and will reverse long-term.
Compromise: ship the new model only to the high-value user segment first, keep everyone else on the old model to watch.
optionExplanations: 先上线再优化护栏，等于先把用户赶跑再补救，流失往往不可逆。
护栏超阈值不是噪声，是明确的体验退化信号，正是它存在的意义。
对；护栏对主指标有否决权，+2% 建立在体验损害上不可持续，应拒绝。
分人群上线不解决体验退化本身，还引入分裂体验和归因难题。
optionExplanations_en: Ship-then-fix means driving users away before repairing, and churn is often irreversible.
A breached guardrail is not noise but a clear degradation signal, which is its entire purpose.
Correct — guardrails veto the primary; a 2% built on UX harm is unsustainable, so reject.
Segmented rollout does not fix the degradation itself and adds split-experience and attribution problems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 任一护栏指标退化超阈值即否决上线，哪怕主指标为正。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guardrail veto means any guardrail regressing past threshold rejects the launch even if the primary metric is positive.

scenario: 新 CTR 模型改变了展示哪些广告，被展示的广告又决定了谁被点击，点击又回流成下一轮训练数据。
scenario_en: A new CTR model changes which ads show, shown ads determine who clicks, and clicks feed back as next-round training data.
q: 为什么反馈回路会让短期 A/B 结论对长期表现不可靠？
q_en: Why do feedback loops make short A/B conclusions unreliable for long-term performance?
why: 模型→改变展示→改变点击→改变未来训练数据，形成自我强化回路。短期 A/B 只看到回路第一圈，测不出多轮迭代后的漂移，所以对长期表现不可靠。
why_en: The model changes what shows, which changes clicks, which changes future training data — a self-reinforcing loop — so a short A/B sees only the first turn and cannot capture drift after many iterations.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  M["新模型"] --> S["改变展示的广告"]
  S --> C["改变点击"]
  C --> D["改变未来训练数据"]
  D --> M
options: 反馈回路和训练数据无关，A/B 短期结论一定等于长期
模型改展示→改点击→改未来训练数据，短测只见回路第一圈
反馈回路只影响延迟，不影响收入结论
只要样本量够大，反馈回路的影响就完全消失
options_en: Feedback loops are unrelated to training data, so short A/B conclusions always equal long-term.
The model changes exposure, then clicks, then future training data; a short test sees only the first turn of that loop.
Feedback loops affect only latency, not revenue conclusions.
With a large enough sample, feedback-loop effects vanish entirely.
optionExplanations: 回路的本质就是当前模型的展示会塑造未来训练数据，短期结论不能外推。
对；自强化回路要多轮才显形，短 A/B 采样不到，需长跑或长期留存监控补足。
回路改的是数据分布和长期点击结构，直接影响收入结论，不只是延迟。
样本量补不了「未来数据被当前模型塑造」这种时间维度的偏差。
optionExplanations_en: The loop's essence is that current exposure shapes future training data, so short conclusions do not extrapolate.
Correct — a self-reinforcing loop only shows over many turns that a short A/B cannot sample, needing long runs or retention monitoring.
The loop changes data distribution and long-term click structure, directly affecting revenue, not just latency.
Sample size cannot fix a time-dimension bias where future data is shaped by the current model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型的展示决策塑造未来训练数据，形成自我强化，使短期实验难反映长期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feedback loop is when the model's exposure decisions shape future training data, self-reinforcing so short tests miss long-term effects.

scenario: 广告定向表面看只是「谁更可能点」，但住房、就业、信贷类广告受法律约束。
scenario_en: Ad targeting looks like just 'who is likely to click,' but housing, employment, and credit ads are legally regulated.
q: 为什么住房/就业/信贷广告的公平性是法律问题而不只是道德问题？
q_en: Why is fairness for housing/employment/credit ads a legal issue, not only a moral one?
why: 这些品类受《公平住房法(FHA)》《平等信贷机会法(ECOA)》等约束：即便定向是「性别中立」的，若模型把工作机会主要投给某一性别，就构成法律风险 + 实质伤害，平台要担责。
why_en: These categories fall under laws like the Fair Housing Act and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, so even gender-neutral targeting that delivers job ads mostly to one gender creates legal liability and real harm.
options: 因为住房/信贷广告的点击率和出价都最高，平台想多赚钱才格外谨慎审核
因为这些广告的特征更新频繁，最容易触发缓存失效，纯属工程问题
因为这类广告的投放链路更长、延迟更高，需要额外做服务优化
受 FHA/ECOA 等法律约束，歧视性投放要担法律责任
options_en: Because housing/credit ads have both the highest CTR and bids, so the platform reviews them extra carefully to earn more.
Because these ads' features update frequently and most easily trigger cache invalidation — a pure engineering concern.
Because this category's delivery path is longer with higher latency, needing extra serving optimization.
Laws such as FHA and ECOA apply, so discriminatory delivery creates legal liability.
optionExplanations: 和点击率高低无关；问题在于这些机会的分配受反歧视法约束。
这不是缓存问题，是投放分布是否公平的合规问题。
延迟是服务话题；这里的关键是法律层面的歧视风险。
对；FHA/ECOA 直接管辖住房、信贷等机会分配，歧视性投放让平台担法律责任。
optionExplanations_en: Unrelated to CTR height; the issue is that allocating these opportunities is governed by anti-discrimination law.
Not a cache issue but a compliance question of whether the delivery distribution is fair.
Latency is a serving topic; the key here is legal discrimination risk.
Correct — FHA/ECOA govern allocation of housing and credit opportunities, so discriminatory delivery makes the platform legally liable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 美国《公平住房法》：禁止在住房相关机会中基于受保护属性歧视。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The FHA (Fair Housing Act) prohibits discrimination in housing-related opportunities based on protected attributes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 美国《平等信贷机会法》：禁止在信贷机会中基于受保护属性歧视。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ECOA (Equal Credit Opportunity Act) prohibits discrimination in credit opportunities based on protected attributes.

scenario: 你要给受监管广告选公平性定义，衡量投放是否歧视。
scenario_en: You must pick a fairness definition for regulated ads to measure whether delivery is discriminatory.
q: 人口统计学平等(demographic parity)和反事实公平(counterfactual fairness)差在哪一维？
q_en: On what dimension do demographic parity and counterfactual fairness differ?
why: 人口统计学平等是群体级：各群体的投放率应相等（如男女看到 SWE 广告比例相当）。反事实公平更严、是因果个体级：如果这个具体用户的种族/性别不同，他还会收到同一广告吗？一个看群体统计，一个看个体因果。
why_en: Demographic parity is group-level (delivery rates equal across groups) while counterfactual fairness is stricter and causal at the individual level (would this specific user get the same ad if their race/gender differed).
tradeoff: 群体级统计平等 vs 个体级因果反事实
options: 平等=群体级投放率相等；反事实=个体级因果反问
两者都是群体级，只是一个看点击、一个看曝光
平等是个体因果，反事实是群体统计，正好相反
两者完全等价，任何模型任何时候都可以同时满足
options_en: Parity is group-level equal delivery rates; counterfactual is an individual-level causal what-if.
Both are group-level, differing only in click vs impression.
Parity is individual causal and counterfactual is group statistics, exactly reversed.
They are fully equivalent, so any model can satisfy both at any time.
optionExplanations: 对；一个是群体投放率相等的统计约束，一个是改属性后个体结果不变的因果约束。
反事实不是群体级，它问的是单个用户在反事实属性下会怎样。
说反了：平等才是群体统计，反事实才是个体因果。
两者常常无法同时满足（下一题），并不等价。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — one is a group statistic of equal delivery rates, the other a causal constraint that an individual's outcome is unchanged if the attribute changes.
Counterfactual is not group-level; it asks what happens to a single user under a counterfactual attribute.
Reversed: parity is the group statistic and counterfactual is the individual causal one.
They often cannot be satisfied simultaneously (next card) and are not equivalent.

termDefinitions.term: demographic parity / 人口统计学平等
termDefinitions.meaning: 又称统计平等：各受保护群体的广告投放率应相等，是群体级公平判据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Demographic (statistical) parity requires equal ad-delivery rates across protected groups, a group-level fairness criterion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 因果个体级判据：若把该用户的受保护属性改掉，结果应不变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Counterfactual fairness is a causal individual criterion: flipping the user's protected attribute should not change the outcome.

scenario: 一条 SWE 招聘广告定向设成「SF 湾区所有 25-45 岁」看似性别中立，实际投放里 80% 是男性。
scenario_en: A SWE job ad targeted 'all 25-45 in the SF Bay Area' looks gender-neutral but is delivered 80% to men.
q: 定向是性别中立的，为什么投放却 80% 男性，哪个判据能抓住？
q_en: Targeting is gender-neutral yet delivery is 80% male — what caused it and which criterion catches it?
why: 模型从特征里学到了与性别相关的相关性（历史点击、职业兴趣等），即使没有显式性别特征，也把广告主要投给男性。人口统计学平等（比较群体投放率）正好能把这种不平衡标出来。
why_en: The model learned feature-to-gender correlations even without a gender feature, so it delivers mostly to men, and demographic parity — comparing group delivery rates — flags this imbalance.
tradeoff: 群体投放率平等（抓分布不均）vs 只看预测分公平（漏掉投放端偏差）
whenOtherWins: 若要追问「这一个具体女性用户是否因性别被区别对待」，群体平等不够，得用反事实公平做个体级因果判断。
options: 定向没写性别就一定公平，80% 男性只是随机波动，无需判据
模型学到与性别相关的特征，人口统计学平等能标出这种不均
只要模型没有显式性别特征，就不可能产生性别倾斜
这只能靠反事实公平发现，群体级判据完全无能为力
options_en: No gender in targeting means it is fair; 80% male is random noise needing no criterion.
The model learned gender-correlated features, and demographic parity flags the imbalance.
Without an explicit gender feature, gender skew is impossible.
Only counterfactual fairness can detect this; group-level criteria are useless here.
optionExplanations: 80% 对 20% 不是随机波动，是系统性倾斜，恰恰需要公平判据来量化。
对；代理相关性让中立定向也倾斜，群体投放率对比直接暴露不均衡。
去掉性别特征不够，其他特征（职业、行为）会作为代理重建性别信号。
群体平等正是抓这种群体不均的合适工具；反事实是补充不是唯一手段。
optionExplanations_en: 80% vs 20% is not noise but systematic skew, exactly what a fairness criterion should quantify.
Correct — proxy correlations skew even neutral targeting, and comparing group delivery rates exposes the imbalance.
Dropping the gender feature is not enough; other features (job, behavior) act as proxies and rebuild the signal.
Group parity is the right tool for group imbalance here; counterfactual is a complement, not the only means.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非受保护特征（职业、行为、地区）与受保护属性高度相关，间接重建了它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A proxy correlation is when non-protected features (job, behavior, geo) correlate with a protected attribute, indirectly rebuilding it.

scenario: 你想让一个投放模型同时满足人口统计学平等和反事实公平。
scenario_en: You want a delivery model to satisfy both demographic parity and counterfactual fairness at once.
q: 为什么同时满足人口统计学平等和反事实公平常常在数学上不可能？
q_en: Why is satisfying both demographic parity and counterfactual fairness often mathematically impossible?
why: 让各群体投放率相等，有时必须按群体区别对待个体（给某群体加权/降权），这恰恰违反「改属性不改结果」的反事实公平。两者常互斥：受监管品类偏向群体平等，个性化场景可能偏反事实。
why_en: Forcing equal group rates can require treating individuals differently by group, which violates counterfactual fairness's 'same outcome if the attribute changed,' so the two often conflict.
options: 因为两者定义完全相同，重复约束导致方程无解
因为反事实公平需要更多 GPU，算力不够所以做不到
强制群体投放率相等要按群体区别对待个体，违反反事实公平
因为法律明确禁止同时使用两个公平判据，只能二选一
options_en: Because the two definitions are identical, so duplicate constraints make the system unsolvable.
Because counterfactual fairness needs more GPUs and there is not enough compute.
Forcing equal group delivery rates requires treating individuals differently by group, violating counterfactual fairness.
Because the law explicitly forbids using two fairness criteria at once, so you must pick one.
optionExplanations: 两者定义不同（群体 vs 个体因果），不是重复约束。
这不是算力问题，是两个判据在数学上互相矛盾。
对；群体拉平往往要求个体级差别对待，直接撞上反事实的「改属性不改结果」。
法律没有禁止；是判据本身数学互斥，需按场景取舍。
optionExplanations_en: The definitions differ (group vs individual causal), so they are not duplicate constraints.
Not a compute issue but a mathematical conflict between the two criteria.
Correct — equalizing groups often demands individual-level differential treatment, colliding with counterfactual's invariance.
The law does not forbid it; the criteria are mathematically incompatible, forcing a context-based choice.

termDefinitions.term: fairness impossibility / 公平不可能性
termDefinitions.meaning: 多个公平判据常无法同时满足，需按场景（受监管 vs 个性化）取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fairness impossibility means multiple fairness criteria often cannot hold together, forcing a context-based tradeoff.

scenario: 你的模型对各群体的预测分看着很公平，但竞价里出价加权会改变谁最终被展示。
scenario_en: Your model's predicted scores look fair across groups, but auction bid weighting changes who ultimately gets shown.
q: 公平性该在「预测分」上算还是在「实际投放分布」上算？
q_en: Should fairness be computed on predicted scores or on the actual delivery distribution?
why: 要在实际投放分布上算：模型分公平，不代表投放公平——竞价的出价加权会把公平的分数变成不公平的投放。只审预测分会漏掉投放端偏差。
why_en: Compute fairness on the delivery distribution, because fair scores do not mean fair delivery — auction bid weighting can turn fair scores into unfair delivery, and auditing scores alone misses it.
tradeoff: 审预测分（漏掉竞价加权偏差）vs 审实际投放分布（抓端到端真实结果）
whenOtherWins: 如果没有竞价/出价加权、预测分直接等于展示决策（如无广告的自然排序），那审预测分和审投放等价。
options: 算预测分就够——模型给出的分数公平，投放结果自然也会跟着公平
两者都不用算，只要模型里没有显式的敏感特征字段就够了
只算点击后的转化率，投放阶段的分布是否公平不需要单独管
算实际投放分布：出价加权会把公平的分变成不公平投放
options_en: Predicted scores alone suffice — if the model's scores are fair, the delivery outcome naturally follows.
Compute neither — as long as the model has no explicit sensitive-feature field, that is enough.
Only compute post-click conversion rate; whether the delivery stage's distribution is fair doesn't need separate tracking.
Compute on actual delivery: bid weighting turns fair scores into unfair delivery.
optionExplanations: 分公平≠投放公平：竞价环节的出价、预算、加权会重塑最终谁被展示。
去掉敏感特征挡不住代理特征，也管不了竞价端的投放偏差。
投放阶段正是偏差发生处，跳过它等于放过最关键的一环。
对；端到端真实结果在投放分布上，只有它能抓住竞价加权引入的不公平。
optionExplanations_en: Fair scores do not equal fair delivery: bids, budgets, and weighting in the auction reshape who is finally shown.
Dropping sensitive features cannot stop proxies nor the delivery-side bias in the auction.
The delivery stage is exactly where bias occurs, so skipping it ignores the most critical step.
Correct — the end-to-end truth is in the delivery distribution, the only place to catch unfairness introduced by bid weighting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告最终实际展示给各群体的分布，反映竞价加权后的端到端结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The delivery distribution is who ads are actually shown to across groups, reflecting end-to-end results after auction weighting.

scenario: 模型里没有种族特征，但用了邮编（zip code）。美国居住存在种族隔离，邮编和种族高度相关。
scenario_en: The model has no race feature but uses zip code; due to residential segregation, zip correlates strongly with race.
q: 没有种族特征，为什么邮编仍会导致按种族相关的投放偏差？
q_en: With no race feature, why can zip code still cause race-correlated delivery bias?
why: 邮编是种族的代理特征：居住隔离让邮编和种族高度相关，模型用邮编就等于间接用了种族，产生按种族相关的投放差异，却没有一个显式「种族」字段可查。
why_en: Zip code is a proxy for race — residential segregation makes them highly correlated — so using zip indirectly uses race and produces race-correlated delivery without any explicit race field.
options: 邮编是种族的代理变量：用邮编等于间接用种族
邮编只影响配送地址，不可能影响广告投放公平
只要不叫「种族」这个字段名，就不存在歧视
邮编和种族在统计上完全无关，这种担忧是多余的
options_en: Zip code is a proxy for race, so using zip indirectly uses race.
Zip only affects shipping address and cannot affect ad-delivery fairness.
As long as the field is not named 'race,' no discrimination exists.
Zip and race are statistically unrelated, so the worry is unnecessary.
optionExplanations: 对；代理特征让隔离的地理信息偷偷携带种族信号，删掉「种族」字段也拦不住。
这里的邮编是模型特征、影响投放决策，不是物流地址。
字段命名无关紧要，重要的是特征是否与受保护属性相关。
居住隔离使邮编与种族高度相关，这是有据可查的代理效应。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the proxy lets segregated geography secretly carry a race signal, which dropping the race field cannot stop.
Here zip is a model feature affecting delivery decisions, not a shipping address.
The field name is irrelevant; what matters is whether the feature correlates with a protected attribute.
Residential segregation makes zip strongly correlate with race, a documented proxy effect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本身非敏感、但与受保护属性高度相关的特征（如邮编↔种族），会间接引入歧视。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A proxy feature is non-sensitive itself but highly correlated with a protected attribute (e.g. zip to race), indirectly introducing discrimination.

scenario: 广告主用兴趣排除列表定向，把「无障碍/辅助工具（accessibility tools）」兴趣排除在受众之外。
scenario_en: An advertiser uses an interest exclusion list to exclude the 'accessibility tools' interest from the audience.
q: 排除「无障碍工具」兴趣这个动作会造成什么歧视后果？
q_en: What discriminatory consequence follows from excluding the 'accessibility tools' interest?
why: 排除「无障碍工具」兴趣，实际上把残障用户过滤掉了——兴趣成了残障状态的代理。类似地，按语言排除会过滤掉少数族裔。排除列表滥用是没有敏感特征也能歧视的典型路径。
why_en: Excluding the accessibility-tools interest effectively filters out disabled users, since the interest proxies disability, just as language-based exclusion filters ethnic minorities.
options: 只是把受众规模缩小了一圈，定向逻辑里没有涉及任何受保护群体
把残障用户过滤掉——兴趣成了残障状态的代理，构成歧视
只是改变了广告预算的消耗速度，跟投放公平性完全无关
会让模型排序的 AUC 略微下降，这只是个纯技术调优问题
options_en: It just shrinks the audience by a bit — the targeting logic doesn't touch any protected group.
It filters out disabled users — the interest proxies disability status — which is discriminatory.
It only changes how fast the ad budget burns, completely unrelated to delivery fairness.
It makes the model's ranking AUC dip slightly — purely a technical tuning issue.
optionExplanations: 缩小受众的说法掩盖了本质：被排除的正是残障这一受保护群体。
对；兴趣是残障的代理，排除它=系统性排除残障用户，语言排除同理过滤少数族裔。
这不是预算问题，是把受保护群体排除在机会之外的公平问题。
AUC 无关；核心是投放对受保护群体的系统性排除。
optionExplanations_en: 'Shrinking the audience' hides the point: the excluded group is precisely disabled, a protected class.
Correct — the interest proxies disability, so excluding it systematically excludes disabled users, as language exclusion filters minorities.
Not a budget issue but a fairness issue of excluding a protected group from opportunity.
AUC is irrelevant; the core is systematic exclusion of a protected group from delivery.

termDefinitions.term: exclusion list abuse / 排除列表滥用
termDefinitions.meaning: 用兴趣/语言排除定向间接筛掉受保护群体，是无敏感特征也能歧视的路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exclusion-list abuse uses interest or language exclusions to indirectly filter out protected groups, discriminating without a sensitive feature.

scenario: 模型纯以 CTR 为目标：把高价值广告（工作/住房/信贷）投给历史上参与度更高的群体，他们的点击又回流成训练数据。
scenario_en: Pure CTR optimization sends high-value ads (jobs/housing/credit) to historically more-engaged groups, whose clicks feed back as training data.
q: 纯 CTR 优化为什么会把机会型广告自我强化地集中给已占优势的群体？
q_en: Why does pure CTR optimization self-amplify high-value ads toward already-advantaged groups?
why: 已占优势群体历史参与度高→模型学到投给他们 CTR 更高→更多投给他们→他们点击更多→回流训练数据进一步强化，形成自我放大回路，把工作/住房/信贷机会越来越集中给优势群体。
why_en: Advantaged groups historically engaged more, so the model learns they yield higher CTR, delivers more to them, they click more, and that feeds back to reinforce the loop, concentrating opportunity ads on the already-privileged.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["优势群体历史参与高"] --> B["模型学到投他们 CTR 高"]
  B --> C["更多机会广告投给他们"]
  C --> D["他们点击更多"]
  D --> A
options: 因为随机分配本身就会天然偏向某个群体，跟优化目标设成什么无关
因为 CTR 优化目标里带了纠偏项，模型训练得越久反而越公平
优势群体历史参与高→模型多投给他们→点击回流，自放大
因为工作/住房这类高价值广告出价更低，平台只投得起优势群体
options_en: Because random allocation itself naturally skews toward some group, regardless of what the objective is set to.
Because the CTR objective already includes a de-biasing term, so the model grows fairer the longer it trains.
Advantaged groups engaged more, so the model delivers more to them and their clicks feed back, amplifying itself.
Because high-value ads like jobs/housing bid lower, so the platform can only afford to deliver them to advantaged groups.
optionExplanations: 偏向不是随机，是优化目标（CTR）系统性追逐历史高参与群体的结果。
纯 CTR 优化没有公平项，只会强化历史模式，不会自动纠偏。
对；这是历史偏差经反馈回路自我放大，需显式公平约束或政策才能打断。
出价高低不是主因；主因是 CTR 目标追逐历史高参与群体并被回路放大。
optionExplanations_en: The skew is not random but the systematic result of chasing historically high-engagement groups via the CTR objective.
Pure CTR optimization has no fairness term and reinforces historical patterns rather than self-correcting.
Correct — historical bias self-amplifies through the feedback loop, needing an explicit fairness constraint or policy to break it.
Bid level is not the main cause; it is the CTR objective chasing high-engagement groups, amplified by the loop.

termDefinitions.term: optimization feedback loop / 优化反馈回路
termDefinitions.meaning: 纯 CTR 目标把机会集中给历史高参与群体，点击回流不断强化，自我放大不平等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An optimization feedback loop concentrates opportunity on historically engaged groups, and their clicks feed back to self-amplify inequality.

scenario: 你要在系统里防止投放歧视，单靠一个环节不够，需要多层缓解。
scenario_en: You must prevent delivery discrimination in the system, and one layer is not enough — you need multi-level mitigations.
q: 哪些属于多层公平性缓解手段？(多选)
q_en: Which are multi-level fairness mitigations? (multiple)
why: 多层缓解：训练层用公平感知正则（对投放率差异加惩罚项）；监控层做事后投放审计 + 分段校准监控（按周/月比较各群体曝光）；政策层限制受监管品类的定向（如住房广告禁用邮编定向）。堆更多 GPU 不解决公平。
why_en: Multi-level mitigations span training (fairness-aware regularization), monitoring (post-hoc delivery audits and per-segment calibration), and policy (restrict targeting for regulated categories), while more GPUs do not address fairness.
options: 训练层：公平感知正则，对群体投放率差异加惩罚项
监控层：事后投放审计 + 分段校准，按周/月比较各群体曝光
政策层：限制受监管品类的定向（如住房广告禁用邮编定向）
算力层：给训练加更多 GPU，让模型更快收敛
options_en: Training: fairness-aware regularization penalizing group delivery-rate disparity.
Monitoring: post-hoc delivery audits plus per-segment calibration, comparing exposure weekly/monthly.
Policy: restrict targeting for regulated categories (e.g. disable zip targeting for housing ads).
Compute: add more GPUs so the model converges faster.
optionExplanations: 对；训练层直接把公平写进损失，惩罚投放率差异，从源头压不均。
对；监控层持续审计投放分布，抓训练时没消掉的漂移。
对；政策层从定向入手，对高风险品类直接禁用危险维度。
错；GPU 只影响训练速度，和投放是否公平毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — training bakes fairness into the loss, penalizing delivery-rate disparity at the source.
Correct — monitoring continuously audits the delivery distribution, catching drift training did not remove.
Correct — policy acts at targeting, disabling dangerous dimensions for high-risk categories.
Incorrect — GPUs affect only training speed, unrelated to whether delivery is fair.

termDefinitions.term: fairness-aware regularization / 公平感知正则
termDefinitions.meaning: 在损失里加一项惩罚群体投放率差异，训练时就压低不公平。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fairness-aware regularization adds a loss term penalizing group delivery-rate disparity, reducing unfairness during training.

scenario: 你想在训练阶段就压低投放不均，而不是等上线后再事后审计补救。
scenario_en: You want to reduce delivery imbalance during training rather than fixing it with post-hoc audits after launch.
q: 训练层该用哪种手段直接压低投放率差异？
q_en: What training-level technique directly reduces delivery-rate disparity?
why: 公平感知正则：在损失函数里加一项惩罚群体投放率差异，训练时就把公平作为目标之一，从源头约束。代价是可能牺牲一点 CTR/收入，是公平和收益的显式取舍。
why_en: Fairness-aware regularization adds a loss term penalizing group delivery-rate disparity so fairness is optimized during training, at the cost of some CTR/revenue — an explicit fairness-vs-yield tradeoff.
tradeoff: 公平感知正则（源头压不均，牺牲一点 CTR）vs 纯 CTR 目标（收益最大但强化偏差）
whenOtherWins: 如果品类不受监管、也无歧视风险（如普通零售促销），可不加公平惩罚、纯以 CTR/收入为目标。
options: 加大学习率，让模型更快收敛就能变公平
只在上线后做事后审计，训练阶段不动
公平感知正则：损失里加惩罚群体投放率差异的项
直接删掉特征里的邮编字段，其他特征和目标都不变
options_en: Increase the learning rate so faster convergence makes it fair.
Only do post-hoc audits after launch, leaving training untouched.
Fairness-aware regularization: add a loss term penalizing group delivery-rate disparity.
Just drop the zip-code feature and leave every other feature and the objective unchanged.
optionExplanations: 学习率是优化超参，和投放是否公平无关，调它不会变公平。
事后审计是监控层，不是训练层的源头约束，问的是训练阶段手段。
对；把公平写进损失是训练层直接手段，代价是可能牺牲少量 CTR。
删邮编挡不住其他代理特征（职业、行为）重建偏差，治标不治本。
optionExplanations_en: Learning rate is an optimization hyperparameter unrelated to delivery fairness.
Post-hoc audit is monitoring, not a training-level source constraint, which is what is asked.
Correct — baking fairness into the loss is the training-level technique, at the cost of some CTR.
Deleting zip cannot stop other proxies (job, behavior) from rebuilding the bias, treating symptoms only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 损失函数里额外一项，把某个不希望的量（这里是投放率差异）往下压。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A regularization penalty is an extra loss term that pushes down an undesired quantity, here delivery-rate disparity.

scenario: 住房类广告受《公平住房法》约束，你想用最直接、可审计的手段降低按地理的种族歧视风险。
scenario_en: Housing ads fall under the Fair Housing Act, and you want the most direct, auditable way to reduce geographic race-discrimination risk.
q: 对住房广告，政策层最直接的缓解是什么？
q_en: For housing ads, what is the most direct policy-level mitigation?
why: 政策层直接禁用高风险定向维度——住房广告禁用邮编定向，因为邮编是种族代理。这比训练层正则更硬、可审计、合规上更稳，代价是牺牲部分定向精度。
why_en: Disable the high-risk targeting dimension outright — no zip-code targeting for housing ads, since zip proxies race — which is harder and more auditable than training-level regularization, at the cost of some targeting precision.
tradeoff: 政策禁用邮编定向（硬约束、可审计，损失定向精度）vs 训练正则（软约束、仍可能残留偏差）
whenOtherWins: 非受监管品类需要精细地理定向（如本地餐饮促销）时，一刀切禁用邮编代价过大，用训练层软约束更合适。
options: 对住房广告禁用邮编定向，因为邮编是种族的代理维度
把住房广告的出价上限统一调高，让所有地区都能看到更多广告
给住房广告单独训练一个参数量更大的专属模型
把住房广告特征的缓存 TTL 从一天缩短到一小时
options_en: Disable zip-code targeting for housing ads because zip is a race proxy dimension.
Uniformly raise the bid cap on housing ads so every region sees more of them.
Train a separate, larger-parameter model dedicated just to housing ads.
Shorten the cache TTL for housing-ad features from one day down to one hour.
optionExplanations: 对；直接禁用代理维度是政策层最硬、可审计的手段，从定向源头切断地理→种族链路。
抬出价只改曝光量，不解决按地理的种族倾斜。
换更大模型不改变代理特征带来的偏差，反而可能更强。
TTL 是服务缓存参数，和投放公平毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — disabling the proxy dimension outright is the hardest, most auditable policy lever, cutting the geo-to-race link at targeting.
Raising bids only changes exposure volume, not the geographic race skew.
A larger model does not remove proxy-driven bias and may even strengthen it.
TTL is a serving-cache parameter, unrelated to delivery fairness.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A targeting restriction is a policy-level hard rule disabling specific targeting dimensions for regulated categories (e.g. no zip for housing).

q: 把广告 CTR 模型上线要过的评估关卡排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the evaluation gates an ad CTR model must pass before launch.
steps: 在线 A/B：RPM 主指标 + 体验护栏，测真实业务影响
离线评估：AUC 看排序、log loss + 校准曲线看概率
公平 + 伦理审查：人口统计学平等/反事实 + 代理特征、排除列表、目标函数
why: 评估是一串闸门：先离线验证模型质量（排序 + 概率），再在线 A/B 验证业务影响（RPM + 护栏），再过公平/伦理审查，全部通过才上线。任何一关不过都不放量。
why_en: Evaluation is a gate chain: offline validates model quality, then online A/B validates business impact, then fairness/ethics review, and only passing all three ships.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["离线: AUC/log loss/校准"] --> B["在线 A/B: RPM+护栏"]
  B --> C["公平+伦理审查"]
  C --> D["放量上线"]

scenario: 校准曲线显示模型整体过自信，你要用事后方法把预测概率拉回和真实频率对齐。
scenario_en: The calibration curve shows overall overconfidence, and you want a post-hoc method to realign predicted probabilities with observed frequency.
q: Platt scaling 和 isotonic regression 是干什么的？
q_en: What do Platt scaling and isotonic regression do?
why: 两者都是事后校准：把已训练模型的原始分重新映射到更贴近真实频率的概率。Platt 用逻辑回归做参数化重映（假设 S 形），isotonic 用单调分段函数（更灵活但需更多数据）。校准曲线用来验证它们是否生效。
why_en: Both are post-hoc calibration that remap a trained model's raw scores to probabilities closer to observed frequency: Platt fits a logistic (S-shaped) mapping, while isotonic fits a flexible monotonic step function needing more data.
options: 它们提升模型的排序 AUC，让正负样本分得更开
事后校准：把原始分重映射到贴近真实频率的概率
它们是两种 A/B 流量切分策略，用于分组实验
它们用来压缩特征向量、降低在线服务延迟
options_en: They raise the model's ranking AUC by separating positives and negatives more.
Post-hoc calibration: remap raw scores to probabilities close to observed frequency.
They are two A/B traffic-splitting strategies used to assign experiment arms.
They compress feature vectors to reduce online serving latency.
optionExplanations: 它们不改排序（AUC 基本不变），只调概率数值使之校准。
对；两者都在训练后重映概率，Platt 参数化、isotonic 非参数更灵活但要更多数据。
和流量切分无关，那是 A/B 设计的话题。
和特征压缩、延迟无关，它们只处理概率校准。
optionExplanations_en: They do not change ranking (AUC is basically unchanged); they adjust probability values to be calibrated.
Correct — both remap probabilities after training: Platt is parametric, isotonic is nonparametric and flexible but needs more data.
Unrelated to traffic splitting, which is an A/B-design topic.
Unrelated to feature compression or latency; they only handle probability calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练完成后把模型原始分重映射到与真实频率对齐的概率，不重训模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Post-hoc calibration remaps a trained model's raw scores to probabilities aligned with observed frequency, without retraining.

scenario: 两个 CTR 模型 A/B，A 组每千次曝光赚 $8、B 组赚 $9，你要用一个可比的收益率下结论。
scenario_en: In an A/B, arm A earns $8 per thousand impressions and arm B earns $9, and you need a comparable yield to conclude.
q: RPM 怎么算、单位是什么、下游用来干什么？
q_en: How is RPM computed, what is its unit, and what does it feed downstream?
why: RPM = Revenue Per Mille = 总收入 / 曝光数 × 1000，单位是每千次曝光收入。它把不同流量规模的收益换算成可比收益率（如 $8 vs $9），是 A/B 收入判定和定价的基数。
why_en: RPM (Revenue Per Mille) = revenue / impressions × 1000, a per-thousand-impressions yield that normalizes traffic into a comparable number driving the A/B revenue verdict.
options: RPM = 每次点击带来的收入，单位是美元/次点击，是计算点击成本的定价指标
RPM = 广告位的总曝光次数，单位是次，只衡量流量规模大小，不是收益指标
RPM = 每千次曝光收入 = 总收入/曝光×1000，是 A/B 的收入主指标
RPM = 模型每秒能处理的请求数，单位是 QPS，是做容量规划用的吞吐指标
options_en: RPM = revenue earned per click, in dollars per click, a pricing metric for cost per click.
RPM = total impression count for an ad slot, in counts, measuring only traffic volume, not revenue.
RPM = revenue per thousand impressions = revenue/impressions×1000, the A/B revenue primary metric.
RPM = requests the model can handle per second, in QPS, a throughput metric for capacity planning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每千次曝光收入 = 总收入 / 曝光数 × 1000，广告变现的可比收益率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPM (Revenue Per Mille) is total revenue over impressions times 1000, a comparable ad-monetization yield.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拉丁语「千」，RPM/CPM 里的 M 就指每千次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Mille is Latin for thousand; the M in RPM/CPM means per thousand.

optionExplanations: 把它当成 CPC 了：CPC 是每次点击收费/收入，按点击计费；RPM 是按千次曝光算，量纲完全不同。
曝光数只是流量规模本身，不是收益率；把「量」和「单位收益」混为一谈，看不出两组谁更赚钱。
对；按千次曝光把不同规模的流量收益拉到同一把尺子上，A/B 里才能直接比 $8 和 $9 谁高。
QPS 是系统吞吐/容量指标，衡量的是请求速率而不是钱，和收益率无关。
optionExplanations_en: That is CPC (cost/revenue per click), billed per click; RPM is billed per thousand impressions, a different unit entirely.
Impression count alone is just traffic volume, not a yield; conflating scale with per-unit revenue hides which arm actually earns more.
Correct — putting revenue on a per-mille basis lines up different traffic scales on one ruler, so $8 vs $9 becomes directly comparable in the A/B.
QPS is a throughput/capacity metric measuring request rate, unrelated to money.
